title: Consistency of linear pairs
examples: What does it mean if a linear pair has no solution?
Can you show me how to use the ratio condition here?
If I get two different answers for k, which one is correct?

explain.say: Today we look at linear pairs of angles. A linear pair of angles always sits on a straight line. This means the angles must add up to one hundred and eighty degrees.
If the angles are in a ratio, we can use letters to represent them. For example, if the ratio is one to two, the angles are x and two times x. We set this up as an equation.
We set the sum of these angles equal to one hundred and eighty degrees. So, x plus two times x equals one hundred and eighty degrees. This lets us find the value of x.
Sometimes, the equation might give us no solution for a variable. This means the angles cannot form a straight line with that ratio. This is an important result to understand.

draw.text: No solution means no angle fits.

faq.q: What is a linear pair of angles?
faq.a: A linear pair of angles are two angles that are next to each other and together form a straight line. They always add up to one hundred and eighty degrees.
asks: What do linear angles add up to?
How many degrees do angles on a straight line make?

faq.q: How do I use a ratio condition in this problem?
faq.a: You assign a variable, like x, to the smallest part of the ratio. Then you write the other angle using that variable and the ratio number. You then solve the equation.
asks: What do I do with the ratio numbers?
Can I use a variable for each angle?

faq.q: What does it mean if I get two different values for the same variable?
faq.a: If you get different values, it usually means there is an error in setting up the equation. Always check that the sum equals one hundred and eighty degrees.
asks: Is it possible to have two answers?
How do I check if my setup is wrong?

faq.q: When do I say there is no solution?
faq.a: You say there is no solution when solving the equation leads to a false statement, like zero equals one hundred. This means the angles cannot exist as described.
asks: What is the opposite of a solution?

faq.q: Does the straight line have to be horizontal?
faq.a: No, the straight line can be in any direction. The key property is that the angles next to each other must sum to one hundred and eighty degrees.
asks: Does the line have to be flat?
Does the orientation matter for the sum?

facts: Angles forming a straight line sum to one hundred and eighty degrees.
A linear pair is composed of two adjacent angles.
If the ratio is m to n, the angles can be represented as mx and nx.
Solving for a variable helps find the measure of the angles.

quiz.say: If two angles in a ratio of one to three form a linear pair, what is the value of the smaller angle?
quiz.why: The angles are x and three times x. Setting up the equation x plus 3x equals one hundred and eighty gives four times x equals one hundred and eighty. Dividing by four gives x, which is the smaller angle, thirty degrees.

wrong.0: This is the answer if you incorrectly assumed the angles were 1:2 and solved for the larger one.
wrong.2: This might happen if you only divide one hundred and eighty by two, forgetting the ratio.
wrong.3: This is the answer if the angles formed a right angle, not a straight line.

quiz.say: Two angles have a ratio of two to five and form a linear pair. What is the value of the larger angle?
quiz.why: The angles are two times x and five times x. Their sum is seven times x equals one hundred and eighty. Solving for x gives one hundred and eighty divided by seven. The larger angle is five times x, which equals one hundred degrees.

wrong.0: This might happen if you incorrectly set the sum to be two hundred and forty degrees.
wrong.1: This is the value of x, not the larger angle itself.
wrong.2: This is the answer if you mistakenly added the ratio numbers two plus five, and then multiplied by ten.

quiz.say: If two angles in a ratio of one to zero form a linear pair, what is the conclusion about the angles?

options.show: One hundred and eighty divided by one
options.say: One hundred and eighty divided by one

quiz.why: The angles are x and zero times x, which is just x. Setting up the equation x plus zero equals one hundred and eighty means x equals one hundred and eighty. However, a ratio of one to zero is impossible for two distinct angles, leading to a contradiction or no valid geometric solution in this context.

wrong.1: This is the sum of the angles, not the conclusion about the ratio.
wrong.2: This incorrectly assumes the smaller angle must be zero.
wrong.3: This incorrectly treats the ratio as a simple division problem.
